observations: Photo 0 shows a black PlayStation 4 console with two controllers on top: one camouflage-patterned and one silver.
The console has 'SONY' and 'PS4' branding visible on the front edge.
The controllers appear to be DualShock 4 models, with the camouflage one having a custom design.
Photo 1 is a similar angle, showing the same console and controllers from a slightly different perspective.
The console is placed on a wooden surface with artificial grass visible in the background.
No visible damage or wear is apparent on the console or controllers in either photo.
The seller claims it is 'hacked with fc26 and 10 other interesting games and one original pad' — this is not visible in the photos.

claims.claim: PlayStation 4 pro hacked with fc26 and 10 other interesting games and one original pad
claims.evidence: No screen or interface is shown to confirm hacking status, FC26 installation, or game list. No original pad is visible — only two controllers, one of which is custom.

risks.risk: Console may not be hacked or may be a non-hacked unit despite seller's claim
risks.proof: Video or photo of the console booting into the system settings or a hacked interface showing FC26 and game list.

risks.risk: Controllers may be non-original or modified, not matching 'one original pad' claim
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the controller ports and labels, or a video showing the controllers being used with the console.

risks.risk: Console may be damaged or have internal issues not visible in photos
risks.proof: Video showing the console powering on, booting, and running a game.

proof_requests: Video of the console booting up and showing the system settings or FC26 interface.
Close-up photo of the controller ports and labels to verify originality.
Video showing the console running a game to confirm functionality.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
